_meta.title: Niche & competition analysis
_meta.headline: The scoring model and its data contract are defined and shipped; the inputs are not, so no niche is ranked and no competition score is published.
_meta.honesty_note: All three fallback redirect targets happened to be air-fryer products in Home & Kitchen. That is NOT a niche signal: it is Amazon's personalised fallback recommendation for the fetching session, it differed per request, and it is unconnected to the submitted identifiers. Nothing was inferred from it.
_meta.score_definition: niche_score = 0.25*commission_index + 0.20*demand_index + 0.20*review_motiveability + 0.15*content_gap + 0.10*price_band_fit + 0.10*(1 - competition_index). Each term is z-scored across the candidate set. Weights are this platform's choice, not an Amazon-supplied formula.

category_rules.caption: Category-level facts that DO constrain niche choice

rows.fact: Commission income for qualifying purchases and programs differs based on product category
rows.impact: Niche choice is materially a category-rate choice; the rate spread is the single highest-leverage input, which is exactly the input that is not public.

rows.fact: Products exclude services other than Amazon Home Services, and the Products Statement carves out Excluded Products (e.g. items sold on a site linked to from an Amazon Site)
rows.impact: Any candidate niche must be checked against the Excluded Products list before content is written, or the work earns nothing.

rows.fact: Pre-release or pre-order products that are not available on a Product listing page are disqualified
rows.impact: Early-access and launch-hype niches — normally the highest-traffic segment for affiliate content — are structurally unmonetisable.

rows.fact: Subscriptions are disqualified unless otherwise provided
rows.impact: Subscription-box and recurring-product niches score zero on commission despite strong apparent LTV.

rows.fact: Digital products do not open the cart-based attribution window the way physical products do
rows.impact: E-books, in-game content and streaming-adjacent offers convert on a much narrower path — deprioritise.

rows.fact: Sites directed toward children, or that knowingly collect personal information from children under 13, are unsuitable
rows.impact: Toys and kids' entertainment are excluded as target niches regardless of demand.

rows.fact: Sites promoting sexually explicit, violent, deceptive or discriminatory content are unsuitable
rows.impact: Screens out the highest-CPC 'grey hat' verticals that affiliate automation usually targets.

rows.fact: Your Site must contain original content; original content using third-party materials must add significant commentary, analysis or transformation
rows.impact: Sets the bar for AI-assisted publishing: bulk restating of Amazon copy is a rejection risk, so generated drafts must be materially additive.

rows.fact: Linking to pages with product lists (search results, events such as Prime Day, department homepages) requires additional original content relevant to the Special Link
rows.impact: Category/roundup pages need editorial substance, not a bare scraped grid of results.

rows.fact: Event links (e.g. Prime Day) are time-bound and the related promotion mentions must be removed as soon as the promotion ends
rows.impact: Seasonal niches need scheduled decay built in, or they silently accumulate policy violations.
